entries.name: Umbrella thorn
entries.voxel_shape: classic flat-topped umbrella crown on a short, often leaning trunk
entries.notes: The defining acacia silhouette of the African savanna; visible for kilometres on open plains.

entries.name: Red oat grass
entries.leaves: narrow paired blades in fire-adapted tussocks
entries.flowers: spiky red-brown panicles in late summer
entries.fire: survives; fire-adapted, seedlings flushes after burns
entries.voxel_shape: dense tussocks that turn the veld maroon in autumn
entries.notes: The dominant tussock of highveld and sourveld; the single best grass block for painting a savanna.

entries.name: African baobab
entries.flowers: white, at night, pollinated by bats
entries.voxel_shape: very thick short trunk, sparse flat crown of root-like branches
entries.notes: A landmark tree: one is visible across the savanna. Trunk stores thousands of litres of water.

entries.name: Fever tree
entries.voxel_shape: smooth lemon-yellow trunk and bare pale branches, sparse crown
entries.notes: Grows in swampy ground, which is why it was linked to 'fevers' (malaria). The yellow trunk is unmistakable.

entries.name: Whistling thorn
entries.voxel_shape: small flat-crowned tree with swollen thorn-base nodules
entries.notes: Swollen galls at the thorn bases house acacia ants that swarm to bite browsers; whistling wind through the thorns gives it its name.

entries.name: Mopane
entries.voxel_shape: butterfly leaves turn copper in autumn; low, flat, sprawling crowns
entries.notes: Defining tree of the mopane veld; hosts the edible mopane worm caterpillar, a protein staple.

entries.name: Marula
entries.flowers: small cream; female trees bear the fruit
entries.voxel_shape: spreading rounded crown, thick grey trunk, drooping branches
entries.notes: Elephants and monkeys strip it for the fermenting fruit; distilled into Amarula cream.

entries.name: Sausage tree
entries.flowers: dark maroon bells on long ropes, bat- and hawkmoth-pollinated
entries.fruit: huge grey sausage pods, inedible raw
entries.voxel_shape: sparse spreading crown with dangling rope-like flowers and 50 cm pods
entries.notes: Unmistakable hanging flowers and fruit; every part poisonous or medicinal, nothing casual here.

entries.name: Camel thorn
entries.fire: survives; reaching roots go 30-60 m deep
entries.voxel_shape: deep-green crown on a thick forked trunk
entries.notes: Roots reach the water table tens of metres down; its presence means deep water nearby.

entries.name: Jackalberry
entries.voxel_shape: dense rounded crown, thick dark trunk, sweet berries
entries.notes: Keystone fruit tree of savanna watercourses; jackals, baboons and hornbills all work it.

entries.name: Leadwood
entries.voxel_shape: pale grey dead-looking bark, sparse small leaves, immovable presence
entries.notes: Extremely dense, termite-proof timber; dead leadwoods stand intact for decades.

entries.name: Buffalo thorn
entries.voxel_shape: tangled zigzag branches armed with paired straight and hooked thorns
entries.notes: Twisted double thorns grab like fish-hooks; the fruit and leaves are eaten across the savanna.

entries.name: Sickle bush
entries.flowers: two-toned spikes, pink above and white below
entries.voxel_shape: dense tangled thicket with pink-and-white bottlebrush flower spikes
entries.notes: Invades overgrazed land and forms impenetrable thickets; the 'wait-a-bit' problem tree.

entries.name: Bermuda grass
entries.leaves: short grey-green blades, matted stolons and rhizomes
entries.voxel_shape: low dense mat covering trampled ground
entries.notes: The trample-proof lawn grass; dominates around bomas, kraals and water points.

entries.name: Guinea grass
entries.leaves: broad arching blades in huge tussocks
entries.voxel_shape: tall arching bunch grass of thicket margins
entries.notes: A moist-savanna bunch grass; cattle chase it, which is why it lines watercourses and thicket edges.

entries.name: Elephant grass
entries.leaves: very tall coarse canes with long blades
entries.voxel_shape: cane-like wall taller than a person
entries.notes: Tall enough to hide a lion; planted as fodder, it escapes into moist watercourses.

entries.name: Thatch grass
entries.leaves: flat blades with prominent white midrib
entries.fire: survives; very flammable, carries the veld fire
entries.voxel_shape: tall golden tussock, silvery when seeding
entries.notes: The classic thatching grass; a ripe stand is a fire waiting to happen.

entries.name: Borassus palm, African palmyra
entries.leaves: evergreen fan palms, huge semicircular fans
entries.flowers: male and female trees separate, tiny on long stalks
entries.fire: survives; thick trunk resists grass fires
entries.voxel_shape: unbranched columnar trunk topped by a fan of rigid semicircular fronds
entries.notes: The palm of the Sahel savanna; sap tapped for palm wine, fans woven into hats and mats.

entries.name: Sycamore fig
entries.flowers: syconia borne on the trunk and branches
entries.fruit: round figs ripening red on the limbs
entries.voxel_shape: massive spreading fig with heavy horizontal limbs shading water
entries.notes: Sacred fig of pharaonic Egypt; a keystone food for hornbills, bats, monkeys and baboons.

entries.name: Natal fig
entries.fruit: small figs, pollinated by a specific wasp
entries.voxel_shape: round-headed fig, often starting as an epiphyte in a host tree
entries.notes: The common bushveld fig; each fig species feeds its own wasp, and the fig wasps feed everyone else.

entries.name: Shea tree
entries.fruit: plum-like drupes; nuts yield shea butter
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled thick-trunked tree with rounded crown and leathery clustered leaves
entries.notes: Shea butter is the cooking and skin fat of the Sahel belt; the trees are protected across farmland.

entries.name: Knobthorn
entries.flowers: brownish bottlebrush spikes, sweet-scented at dusk
entries.voxel_shape: dark rough trunk with knobby protuberances, flat spreading crown
entries.notes: Dusk-scented chocolate-sweet flowers feed nectar bats; knobs on the trunk betray it instantly.

entries.name: Wait-a-bit thorn
entries.voxel_shape: impenetrable cage of hooked thorns
entries.notes: Hooked thorns snatch at you and will not let go until you 'wait a bit'; a natural barrier hedge.

entries.name: Wild olive
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled silvery-leaved small tree, dense and wind-sculpted
entries.notes: Silvery small-leaved olive of the savanna edge; fruit edible only after pickling.

entries.name: Desert date
entries.voxel_shape: spiny grey-green tree, sparse crown, sweet fruit
entries.notes: Every part of this Sahel tree is used: dates, seed oil, soap bark, even medicine.

entries.name: Mountain aloe
entries.leaves: evergreen rosettes of huge spiny-edged blades
entries.flowers: orange-yellow spikes in winter; sunbird nectar
entries.voxel_shape: bare trunk topped by one crowning rosette of huge spiny leaves
entries.notes: A crowned snake of a plant; winter flower spikes hum with sunbirds.

entries.name: Candelabra euphorbia
entries.flowers: small yellow cyathia at stem tips
entries.voxel_shape: columnar cactus impersonator, multiple fingered arms
entries.notes: Not a cactus; the milky latex blisters skin on contact, so it is planted as a living hedge.

entries.name: Kalahari melon
entries.fruit: striped melons; wild form bitter, ancestor of the watermelon
entries.voxel_shape: trailing vine sprawled over bare sand
entries.notes: The wild watermelon; in the dry season it is the only free water for desert game.

entries.name: Devil's claw
entries.growth: fast in the rains, dormant in the dry season
entries.fruit: clawed grapples that hitch onto animals
entries.voxel_shape: prostrate stems radiating from buried tubers, grapple fruits
entries.notes: Harvested for a back-pain remedy; the woody grapples are the most annoying thing on a boot.

entries.name: Devil's thorn
entries.voxel_shape: flat sprawling mat hugging the ground
entries.notes: Follows disturbed ground; the spines puncture tyres, sandals and hooves alike.

entries.name: Red hot poker
entries.voxel_shape: green strap tuft with a flaming torch stem
entries.notes: Torch-like spikes that go from red to yellow as they open; sunbird magnet.

entries.name: Common sugarbush
entries.leaves: evergreen, leathery, clustered at twig tips
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled shrub to small tree with pink-centred sugarbushes
entries.notes: The savanna's own protea; a true resprouter — burn it and it comes back from the base.

entries.name: Lion's tail
entries.flowers: vivid orange whorls stacked like a lion's tail
entries.voxel_shape: stiff stems ringed with orange whorls
entries.notes: Striking rings of orange; a garden escape that naturalises along savanna roadsides.

entries.name: Wild sage, camphor bush
entries.voxel_shape: grey fuzzy mound-shaped bush
entries.notes: Crushed leaves smell of camphor; smoked in shelters to chase insects off.

entries.name: Termite mound mushroom
entries.growth: flushes in days after the rains
entries.fire: n/a; fruits from the termite garden after rain
entries.voxel_shape: grey-white parasol erupting from a termite mound
entries.notes: Grown by termites in their fungus gardens; the biggest are harvested fresh and sold roadside after the rains.

entries.name: Boab
entries.voxel_shape: bottle-shaped trunk with a stubby crown; sometimes hollow
entries.notes: Australia's only baobab, endemic to the Kimberley; sacred trees carry Aboriginal rock paintings.

entries.name: Darwin woollybutt
entries.flowers: orange-scarlet clusters; a honking hornbill tree
entries.voxel_shape: tall pale-trunked gum with woolly grey base and scarlet flower bursts
entries.notes: The flame-flowered gum of Darwin's tropical savannas; honeyeaters and lorikeets riot in the flowering season.

entries.name: Makalani palm
entries.leaves: evergreen, stiff palmate fans, often forked trunk
entries.fruit: woody nuts; the ivory palm of carvers
entries.fire: survives; thick trunk and fan crown resist
entries.voxel_shape: slender forked palm with round fan fronds
entries.notes: The Kalahari's doum palm; its rock-hard nuts are carved like ivory, and the sap ferments into wine.
